s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive respiratory distress with pleural effusion and mediastino-pulmonary mass
salient_findings: Mediastino-pulmonary mass in the left upper lobe
key_facts: 40-year-old woman
One month postpartum
No significant past medical history
Three weeks of symptoms
Left chest pain
Dry cough
Progressive dyspnea
Signs of left pleural effusion on examination
Homogeneous opacity occupying the entire left hemithorax on chest radiograph
Mediastinal shift to the right
Serial thoracenteses produced approximately 2 L of serous fluid every three days
Large pleural effusion on thoracic ultrasonography
Non-diagnostic pleural biopsy
104 × 102 × 141 mm mediastino-pulmonary mass on contrast-enhanced CT
Mass contacts the subclavian artery and lateral border of the aorta
Mass encases a branch of the left pulmonary artery
Endobronchial lesion in the left upper-lobe bronchus on bronchoscopic examination
Non-contributory endobronchial biopsies on two occasions

shortlist.label: Non-small cell lung cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Large mediastino-pulmonary mass and pleural effusion

shortlist.label: Small cell lung cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of symptoms and large tumor size

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms and large mediastino-pulmonary mass

shortlist.label: Pancoast tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Location of the mass in the left upper lobe and symptoms of chest pain and dyspnea

shortlist.label: Mesothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Pleural effusion and large mediastino-pulmonary mass in a patient with no significant past medical history

raw.rationale: The presence of a large mediastino-pulmonary mass, pleural effusion, and an endobronchial lesion in the left upper-lobe bronchus, along with the patient's progressive symptoms, are highly suggestive of a malignant process, with non-small cell lung cancer being a common cause of such findings.

rejected.label: Small cell lung cancer
rejected.why: While possible, small cell lung cancer tends to be more aggressive and centrally located, often with widespread disease at presentation, which is not explicitly indicated here.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma could present with a mass and pleural effusion, but the endobronchial lesion and the specific location and description of the mass are more typical of lung cancer.

rejected.label: Pancoast tumor
rejected.why: A Pancoast tumor is a type of lung cancer, but it specifically involves the apex of the lung and is associated with distinct symptoms such as shoulder pain and Horner's syndrome, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Mesothelioma
rejected.why: Mesothelioma is a possibility with pleural effusion and a mass, but it typically presents with a longer history of asbestos exposure and more diffuse pleural involvement, which is not indicated here.
